findings.title: Dependencies not installed — install required before review
findings.explanation: The node_modules directory is missing. Turpan cannot run build, test, lint, or typecheck without first installing dependencies. Run your package manager install command before re-running the review, or pass the --install flag to have Turpan install automatically (if configured).

evidence.label: Missing node_modules
evidence.excerpt: Directory not found — node_modules is missing

findings.title: Missing test script in package.json
findings.explanation: No `test` script was detected in package.json. The test stage will be skipped without a test command.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a "test" script to package.json, e.g. "test": "vitest" or "test": "jest"

findings.title: MCP server allows arbitrary shell execution: child_process with shell in src/server.ts
findings.explanation: The MCP server in "src/server.ts" executes shell commands. MCP servers with shell access can be exploited to run arbitrary commands on the host if any tool input is user-controlled. This is a CRITICAL security risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove shell execution from MCP tools. If shell access is required, validate input against an explicit allowlist and use parameterized commands (no shell=True). Consider if a native API call can replace the shell command.

findings.title: MCP tool has overly broad schema: unconstrained object schema in src/server.ts
findings.explanation: The MCP tool in "src/server.ts" has an input schema with unconstrained object schema. This provides no guidance to LLM clients about valid inputs, leading to malformed requests and runtime errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Define precise JSON Schema types for all tool inputs: specify required fields, property types (string/number/boolean), string formats (e.g., format: 'uri'), and enum constraints where applicable.
